account:
Today I have been following my appointments. The secretary reported no new correspondence and, after I supplied a writable book, recorded an addendum confirming the builder's eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection. The builder wants me to check the completed lighting. My neighbour confirmed our usual fifteen hundred tea at the dockside cottage. Lunch at home is due at noon, followed by council letters at thirteen and office time at sixteen-thirty.

I reached the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection. The intended checks are grain quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns. I have asked for the miller and looked nearby, but have not located the miller or obtained stock figures or findings. The mill stall advertises hay bales at two emeralds; that alone does not establish the state of supplies.

The unusual thing is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 01 and 11 mentioned it when I arrived. Asked for news, Townsfolk 11 associated the story with the baker, innkeeper, and neighbour, but gave no clear proposal or explanation. My earlier written briefing explicitly described this as an unconfirmed rumour, and the secretary has received no actual proposal. I therefore do not know whether any change is planned, who originated the story, or what purpose it would serve. It may simply be circulating gossip; I should seek a direct account rather than treat repetition as confirmation. I have told the nearby townsfolk that it remains unconfirmed.
